page: Microsoft Azure D8plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by an 8-core Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor running at a dedicated 3.0 GHz clock speed. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance allocates one physical core per vCPU with no hyperthreading, providing predictable compute performance. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a 307 GB local SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 14501.82 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6013.0. Memory subsystem testing shows a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 565.84 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write speeds reach 84.32 GB/sec and 43.64 GB/sec, respectively. Single-core performance is a relative weakness, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1057.0 and a weak Passmark CPU score of 6130.18. Cryptographic performance is also limited, with a Passmark encryption score of 1295.58, reflecting the lack of advanced vector and matrix extensions.

With its dedicated ARM cores and local SSD storage, the D8plds_v5 offers a cost-efficient profile for scale-out workloads that do not require high memory density. It is well-suited for static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 9.92 GB/sec, and database operations, processing 10.26 million Redis SET operations per second. However, it is poorly suited for memory-intensive applications, heavy cryptographic tasks, or large language model inference, where text generation speeds for a 7B model drop to 7.58 tokens/sec.
description: Microsoft Azure D8plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor at 3.0 GHz. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a 307 GB local SSD. Benchmark results show average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14501.82 and a static web serving throughput of 9.92 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is weak, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1057.0, and the lack of advanced vector extensions limits cryptographic and LLM inference workloads. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for scale-out, compute-bound tasks, static web serving, and lightweight database operations like Redis, which registers 10.26 million SET operations per second, but is constrained for memory-heavy or complex mathematical applications.
